title: There is a Game in Your Bug
problem: Top-5 finish in Survive Game Jam 2021. A retro puzzle game where the rules of the game shift dynamically mid-play — designed, built, and shipped within a 48-hour window with a team of 4.
achievements: Top 5 finish in Survive Game Jam 2021 out of hundreds of entries
Built and shipped in 48 hours with a team of 4
Dynamic rule-shifting mechanic designed and implemented entirely within the jam window
body:
A retro puzzle game where the rules of the game change dynamically as you play. Built in 48 hours for Survive Game Jam 2021, where it placed in the Top 5.

The core mechanic — rules shifting mid-play — required designing systems that could be safely swapped at runtime without breaking game state. The challenge was keeping the player informed of what changed without interrupting flow.

title: Car Driving Multiplayer
problem: A live multiplayer mobile simulation game shipped on Android and iOS. I own the rendering pipeline, core gameplay architecture, and the internal tooling that keeps the design team's pipeline efficient — maintaining a production codebase serving real players.
achievements: Drove rendering optimisation — mesh batching, draw call reduction, LOD tuning — to hold frame rate on mid-range Android devices, the primary hardware constraint
Designed and shipped core gameplay systems (car selection, career progression, session management) running live in production
Engineered a custom Unity Editor tooling suite that cut designer iteration time by 70% and eliminated the recurring data-entry errors that previously blocked sprint completion
Kept memory footprint in check across Android and iOS using asset streaming and aggressive object pooling, maintaining stable performance on constrained hardware
body:
Car Driving Multiplayer is a Unity-based mobile simulation game developed at Appsoleut Games, where I have been a core contributor since December 2023. The game is live on Android and iOS.

Performance Work

Mobile targets demand tight frame budgets on hardware ranging from flagship to mid-range. My focus was on the rendering pipeline: static mesh batching to cut draw calls, LOD configuration for vehicles and environment, and memory profiling to catch allocation spikes during gameplay transitions.

Gameplay Systems

I built and iterated on several core systems — car selection and unlock progression, multiplayer session management, and cross-device feature parity. Each system was designed for maintainability so future designers and engineers could extend it without breaking existing behaviour.

Editor Tooling

Designers needed to configure car stats, XP curves, and tuning parameters across dozens of vehicles. I built a custom Unity Editor window that made batch edits safe and reviewable, cutting a 3-hour manual process to under 30 minutes per sprint.

title: Twinn Create — Runtime Mesh Editor
problem: Commercial Unity product requiring real-time geometry manipulation and a live interior visualiser. I built the core mesh editing system and the material preview pipeline — two systems that needed to be fast, non-destructive, and reliable in a production design tool.
achievements: Engineered runtime mesh editing — extrude, flip, and parametric controls — by directly manipulating Unity mesh data structures, enabling non-destructive geometry editing in a live product
Built the real-time material and furniture preview system powering Twinn Vision's interior design experience — instant feedback with no bake step
Developed internal debugging tooling for the Computer Vision team to detect and visualise scene data misalignment, replacing a manual inspection process
Authored custom surface shaders in Shader Graph and built responsive in-app toolbars using UI Toolkit, maintaining visual quality across target screen resolutions
body:
At Tooliqa I was a core engineer on two commercial Unity products: Twinn Create (a design and modelling tool) and Twinn Vision (a real-time interior visualiser).

Runtime Mesh Editing

Twinn Create required users to manipulate 3D geometry at runtime — extruding faces, flipping normals, and adjusting parametric dimensions. I implemented these operations by directly reading and writing Unity Mesh data structures, handling winding order, UV re-projection, and normal recalculation after each edit.

Twinn Vision — Material & Furniture Preview

The visualiser needed real-time material swaps (texture, colour, roughness) and furniture model swapping within a pre-built scene. I built the preview pipeline using Shader Graph for the material previews and a scene management layer for asset loading and placement.

CV Debugging Tools

The Computer Vision team worked with spatial data that frequently had alignment errors when imported into Unity scenes. I built a set of Unity Editor tools that visualised misalignment, let engineers mark and correct bad data, and validated the fixed output — reducing their QA iteration cycle significantly.

title: Car Tuning Tool
problem: The design team was spending hours each sprint manually editing car stats and balance data across dozens of ScriptableObjects — fragile, slow, and impossible to audit. I designed and built a Unity Editor tooling suite to automate the entire pipeline.
achievements: Custom Unity Editor window with batch-edit workflows for all car balance parameters
CSV ↔ ScriptableObject sync pipeline with validation and rollback
Property drawers and inspector drawers for non-technical designers
Reduced content iteration time by 70% — design changes that took 3 hours now take under 30 minutes
metrics: Zero data-entry errors post-launch (previously ~5 per sprint)
body:
At Appsoleut Games, the car tuning system required frequent balance updates across dozens of vehicles. Each update meant manually editing ScriptableObjects in the Unity inspector — a process that took hours and regularly introduced errors.

The Problem

The data was split across many ScriptableObjects with deeply nested fields. Non-technical designers couldn't safely edit them directly, so every balance change required an engineer. The feedback loop was painfully slow.

The Solution

I built a custom Unity Editor window that loads all car data into an editable spreadsheet-style view. Designers can edit values inline, batch-apply changes across multiple cars, and preview the outcome before committing. A validation pass flags out-of-range values before any write occurs.

CSV Pipeline

The tool also supports CSV import and export. The design team maintains the canonical balance data in a shared Google Sheet. Importing the CSV into Unity syncs all ScriptableObjects in one click, with a diff view showing what changed. Exporting lets them share the live game data back to the sheet.

title: Rage - The Game
problem: Top-20 finish at BYOG 2021 (Build Your Own Game). A puzzle-platformer where players navigate increasingly complex levels to reach a wormhole — designed and shipped from scratch within the 48-hour jam window.
achievements: Top-20 finish in BYOG (Build Your Own Game) 2021
Designed and shipped a complete puzzle-platformer — level progression, physics, and win conditions — within the 48-hour jam window
Built entirely from scratch with no pre-made templates or assets
body:
Rage - The Game is a puzzle-platformer built for BYOG (Build Your Own Game) 2021, where it placed in the Top 20. Players navigate each level to find and reach a wormhole, with level design that escalates in complexity as the game progresses.

The jam constraint pushed rapid prototyping — designing, building, and balancing levels within a 48-hour window required tight scope and quick iteration on feel.

title: VR / AR Medical Visualisation
problem: XR engineering internship at AiSolve Limited. Two parallel workstreams: porting a VR anatomy quiz to a new hardware platform, and expanding an AR heart anatomy visualisation with interactive educational content.
achievements: Successfully ported a VR anatomy quiz from HTC Vive to Oculus Quest using Unity XR Toolkit, resolving SDK-level differences and remapping platform-specific input
Profiled and optimised the ported scene to reach stable frame rate on Quest's standalone hardware — within the performance budget needed for comfortable VR
Extended the AR/MR heart anatomy experience with interactive annotation layers and educational content modules requested by the client
Integrated analytics instrumentation and coordinated delivery directly with the client — full ownership from spec to production
body:
During my internship at AiSolve Limited, I worked on two XR projects for healthcare and education clients.

VR Quiz Port (HTC Vive → Oculus Quest)

The existing VR anatomy quiz was built for PC-tethered HTC Vive hardware. Porting to standalone Oculus Quest required adapting the input system (from SteamVR to Oculus SDK / Unity XR Toolkit), re-optimising the scene for standalone GPU constraints, and fixing controller-specific UI interaction logic. After profiling the ported build on device, I made targeted draw call and texture compression changes to reach stable performance.

AR/MR Heart Visualisation

The second project was an augmented reality application for medical education, visualising the human heart overlaid on the real world. I added interactive educational content layers — labels, annotations, and guided interactions — and helped integrate the analytics system that tracked user engagement with each content section.

title: Untitled Ghost Game
problem: A game jam project where players switch between human and ghost states to overcome obstacles — each form has distinct physics behaviour and interaction rules. Placed Top 5 and was invited to showcase at an industry event.
achievements: Designed and implemented a dual-form mechanic with fully distinct physics and interaction systems per state — core to all of the game's puzzle design
Invited to showcase at an industry event as a Top 5 game
Shipped a complete, polished experience within the jam's 48-hour constraints
body:
A game jam project built around a dual-form mechanic: players switch between a solid human form and an intangible ghost form to navigate obstacles. Each form interacts with the environment differently — the human obeys normal physics and can push objects; the ghost passes through certain surfaces but cannot interact with physical elements.

The game was invited to be showcased to industry leaders as a Top 5 entry.
